answer: Sybil resistance comes from making coordinated equivocation costly: if k identities sign conflicting histories, pairwise evidence yields penalties proportional to k(k−1)/2, or O(k²), rather than a flat per-identity fee. Bonded collateral and asymmetric depreciation amplify detection costs; a swarm’s aggregate loss can carry an exponential multiplier with its size, making duplicated control riskier than honest participation. An echo across a bridge or willow network still leaves attributable evidence.
